newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle steady $67, light -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle steady $67, light -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle on Friday sold at $67.00 per cwt in light volume, steady with Thursday and down $1.00 from the top price paid on Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
About 300 head traded in Kansas following weekly sales of 88,800 head, including 16,500 head or about 19 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA reported.
About 2,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle following a weekly movement of 118,200, USDA said. This week's showlists were largely depleted, the feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle next week were seen priced mostly at $68.00, with a few at $69.00, underpinned by extremely current feedlot marketings, they said.
Packer demand next week, however, could be spotty following hefty purchases of cattle this week, which should supply beef processors with adequate live inventory, the feedlot sources said.
Beef prices on Friday were quoted up $0.56 to $0.95 per cwt for choice and unchanged to down $0.04 for select, USDA said. There were 227 fabricated beef loads sold.
